subject: math.GT
name: Smooth four-dimensional Poincaré conjecture
statement: Is every closed smooth four-manifold homotopy equivalent to S^4 diffeomorphic to the standard S^4?
importance: It asks whether the simplest topological four-manifold can carry an exotic smooth structure.
status_note: The topological four-dimensional Poincaré theorem is proved; the smooth question in dimension four remains open.

subject: math.GT
name: Smooth four-dimensional Schoenflies conjecture
statement: Does every smooth embedding S^3 into S^4 separate S^4 into two manifolds each diffeomorphic to the standard four-ball?
importance: It controls the relation between embedded spheres, smooth balls, and exotic four-dimensional topology.
status_note: The locally flat topological version and the smooth versions outside the exceptional four-dimensional case are known.

subject: math.GT
name: Exotic smooth structures on the complex projective plane
statement: Does the topological manifold CP^2 admit a smooth structure not diffeomorphic to its standard complex smooth structure?
importance: CP^2 is a basic test case for the limits of smooth four-manifold classification.
status_note: Exotic structures are known on many blowups and on manifolds with larger intersection forms; their existence on CP^2 itself is unresolved.

subject: math.GT
name: Andrews–Curtis conjecture
statement: Can every balanced finite presentation of the trivial group be transformed to the standard trivial presentation using Nielsen moves on relators and conjugation of individual relators?
importance: It connects group presentations to handle cancellation and smooth four-dimensional topology.
status_note: Several candidate counterexamples remain unverified; variants allowing stabilization are separate questions.

subject: math.GT
name: Slice–ribbon conjecture
statement: Is every knot in S^3 that bounds a smoothly embedded disk in B^4 a ribbon knot?
importance: It would give a three-dimensional description of a fundamental four-dimensional knot property.
status_note: This is the smooth statement; topologically slice knots are not all ribbon. Known special classes and proposed counterexamples do not settle the general smooth question.

subject: math.GT
name: Cabling conjecture
statement: If Dehn surgery on a nontrivial knot in S^3 yields a reducible three-manifold, must the knot be a torus knot or a cable knot (including a cable of the unknot), with surgery at the corresponding cabling slope?
importance: It predicts exactly how reducible manifolds can arise through knot surgery.
status_note: The question concerns surgery on knots in S^3; many families, including satellite subcases, are understood.

subject: math.GT
name: Purely cosmetic surgery conjecture
statement: For a nontrivial knot in S^3, can surgeries along two distinct slopes ever produce orientation-preservingly homeomorphic three-manifolds?
importance: It asks how much a filled three-manifold remembers the slope used to construct it.
status_note: Orientation-reversing cosmetic surgeries can occur and are excluded; strong restrictions on possible orientation-preserving pairs are known.

references.title: The purely cosmetic surgery conjecture is true for the Kinoshita-Terasaka and Conway knot families

subject: math.GT
name: Generalized Property R conjecture
statement: If zero-framed surgery on an n-component link in S^3 gives the connected sum of n copies of S^1 × S^2, can the framed link be changed by handle slides to the zero-framed n-component unlink?
importance: It links surgery descriptions of three-manifolds with handle decompositions of four-manifolds.
status_note: The one-component case is Gabai’s Property R theorem; the general question for n at least two is open.

subject: math.GT
name: Berge conjecture on lens-space surgeries
statement: Is every knot in S^3 admitting a nontrivial Dehn surgery to a lens space a doubly primitive knot in Berge’s families?
importance: It seeks a complete classification of one of the most constrained exceptional surgeries.
status_note: The corresponding classification of which lens spaces arise is known in substantial form; classifying all surgery knots remains open.

subject: math.GT
name: Volume conjecture for hyperbolic knots
statement: For every hyperbolic knot K in S^3, does lim as N tends to infinity of (2π/N) log |J_N(K; exp(2πi/N))| equal the hyperbolic volume of S^3 minus K, with J_N normalized to be 1 on the unknot?
importance: It predicts that quantum knot invariants recover classical hyperbolic geometry.
status_note: The limit is proved for particular knots, including the figure-eight knot, but not for all hyperbolic knots.
